response.answer:
## Cómo reduce QLoRA la memoria del ajuste fino

### El punto de partida

El problema que QLoRA ataca es de escala: el ajuste fino estándar en 16 bits de un modelo LLaMA de 65B parámetros exige más de 780 GB de memoria de GPU ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A1)). Las técnicas de cuantización previas reducían la huella de memoria, pero solo servían para inferencia y se rompían durante el entrenamiento ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A1)). La contribución central de QLoRA es demostrar por primera vez que es posible ajustar un modelo cuantizado a 4 bits sin degradación de rendimiento ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A0)).

### El mecanismo: almacenar en 4 bits, calcular en 16

QLoRA retropropaga gradientes a través de un modelo preentrenado **congelado y cuantizado a 4 bits** hacia adaptadores de bajo rango LoRA ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A0)). El truco es separar el tipo de dato de almacenamiento del de cómputo: QLoRA tiene un tipo de almacenamiento de baja precisión (habitualmente 4 bits) y un tipo de cómputo (habitualmente BFloat16); en la práctica, «whenever a QLORA weight tensor is used, we dequantize the tensor to BFloat16, and then perform a matrix multiplication in 16-bit» ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A6)). Solo el pequeño conjunto de pesos adaptadores es lo que se aprende ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A1)).

### Los tres componentes que ahorran memoria

1. **NormalFloat de 4 bits (NF4)**, presentado como un tipo de dato informacionalmente óptimo para pesos distribuidos normalmente ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A0)). Se apoya en la cuantización por cuantiles, que garantiza que cada intervalo de cuantización reciba el mismo número de valores del tensor de entrada, y cuya limitación declarada es el propio proceso de estimación de cuantiles ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A6)).
2. **Doble cuantización**, que cuantiza las constantes de cuantización y ahorra en promedio unos 0,37 bits por parámetro (aproximadamente 3 GB en un modelo de 65B) ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A3)).
3. **Optimizadores paginados (Paged Optimizers)**, cuyo objetivo explícito es evitar que los picos de memoria del *gradient checkpointing* provoquen errores de memoria agotada, que tradicionalmente dificultaban el ajuste en una sola máquina ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A0)).

### Dónde está realmente la memoria: un matiz importante

El artículo ofrece un desglose que matiza la intuición de que «menos parámetros LoRA = menos memoria». El *footprint* total es de 567 MB mientras los parámetros LoRA ocupan solo 26 MB; con *gradient checkpointing*, los gradientes de entrada bajan a unos 18 MB por secuencia, lo que los hace **más intensivos en memoria que todos los pesos LoRA combinados**; en comparación, el modelo base en 4 bits consume 5.048 MB ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A6)). De ahí dos conclusiones del propio texto: el *gradient checkpointing* es importante, y reducir agresivamente la cantidad de parámetros LoRA solo produce beneficios de memoria menores — lo que permite usar más adaptadores sin aumentar significativamente la huella de entrenamiento ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A6)).

### Resultado declarado

QLoRA reduce los requisitos medios de memoria del ajuste fino de un modelo de 65B de más de 780 GB a menos de 48 GB, sin degradar el rendimiento de ejecución ni la predicción respecto a una línea base ajustada por completo en 16 bits ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A1)), lo que permite ajustar un modelo de 65B en una sola GPU de 48 GB conservando el rendimiento de 16 bits ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A0)). Su familia Guanaco alcanza el 99,3 % del nivel de ChatGPT con 24 horas de ajuste en una sola GPU ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A0)). En el desglose por tamaños: Guanaco 65B ocupa 41 GB, 33B unos 21 GB, y Guanaco 13B y 7B bajan a 10 GB y 5 GB ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A57)).

### El contraste con LoRA (la base sobre la que se construye)

LoRA congelaba ya los pesos preentrenados e inyectaba matrices de descomposición de rango entrenables en cada capa del Transformer, reduciendo los parámetros entrenables y la memoria de GPU ([Hu et al., 2021](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3A3988ab1c7f3e96f08c15d84b27753ea4b014054073851c3b70895e4791e2a4f2%3A0)). Con GPT-3 175B y Adam, eso significó reducir los parámetros entrenables 10.000 veces y la memoria de GPU 3 veces, sin latencia adicional en inferencia ([Hu et al., 2021](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3A3988ab1c7f3e96f08c15d84b27753ea4b014054073851c3b70895e4791e2a4f2%3A0)); el consumo de VRAM en entrenamiento pasó de 1,2 TB a 350 GB y el tamaño del *checkpoint* de 350 GB a 35 MB, con un 25 % de aceleración ([Hu et al., 2021](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3A3988ab1c7f3e96f08c15d84b27753ea4b014054073851c3b70895e4791e2a4f2%3A11)). La diferencia clave es que QLoRA añade la cuantización a 4 bits del modelo congelado y los optimizadores paginados **encima** de ese esquema ([Dettmers et al., 2023](nodus://passage/documentary%3Aceff5ff2fe984d354a67c9beca56fac646a915261fbc953a5751905e8559348c%3Af812148533f6082cbfa5b620f8d2cbc2a4e086cd66ddeebdc94c5e46ed1e8b33%3A3)). Ambas obras coinciden en el diagnóstico —el ajuste completo es inviable a escala— y difieren en la palanca: LoRA ataca el número de parámetros entrenables; QLoRA ataca además la precisión de almacenamiento del modelo base.

### Nota de alcance

La selección consultada incluye un buen número de fuentes que no guardan relación con esta pregunta (archivos sintéticos sobre un sensor «Alba», un ensayo «Vega» sobre recuperación espaciada y un estudio «Bruma», entre otros); solo los dos artículos técnicos son pertinentes y son los que sostienen todo lo anterior. Las secciones de contradicciones y de huecos de investigación de esta selección están vacías, de modo que no hay refutaciones documentadas que reportar. La búsqueda se marcó como posiblemente incompleta; conviene tenerlo presente si se quiere ampliar a otras obras sobre cuantización.

# QLORA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs Tim Dettmers∗ Artidoro Pagnoni∗ Ari Holtzman Luke Zettlemoyer University of Washington {dettmers,artidoro,ahai,lsz}@cs.washington.edu ## Abstract We present QLORA, an efficient finetuning approach that reduces memory usage enough to finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning task performance. QLORA backpropagates gradients through a frozen, 4-bit quantized pretrained language model into Low Rank Adapters (LoRA). Our best model family, which we name Guanaco, outperforms all previous openly released models on the Vicuna benchmark, reaching 99.3% of the performance level of ChatGPT while only requiring 24 hours of finetuning on a single GPU. QLORA introduces a number of innovations to save memory without sacrificing performance: (a) 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4), a new data type that is information theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights (b) Double Quantization to reduce the average memory footprint by quantizing the quantization constants, and (c) Paged Optimizers to manage memory spikes. We use QLORA to finetune more than 1,000 models, providing a detailed analysis of instruction following and chatbot performance across 8 instruction datasets, multiple model types (LLaMA, T5), and model scales that would be infeasible to run with regular finetuning (e.g. 33B and 65B parameter models). Our results show that QLoRA finetuning on a small high-quality dataset leads to state-of-the-art results, even when using smaller models than the previous SoTA. We provide a detailed analysis of chatbot performance based on both human and GPT-4 evaluations showing that GPT-4 evaluations are a cheap and reasonable alternative to human evaluation. Furthermore, we find that current chatbot benchmarks are not trustworthy to accurately evaluate the performance levels of chatbots. A lemon-picked analysis demonstrates where Guanaco fails compared to

Edward Hu∗ Yelong Shen∗ Phillip Wallis Zeyuan Allen-Zhu Yuanzhi Li Shean Wang Lu Wang Weizhu Chen yuanzhil, swang, luw, wzchen}@microsoft.com An important paradigm of natural language processing consists of large-scale pretraining on general domain data and adaptation to particular tasks or domains. As we pre-train larger models, full fine-tuning, which retrains all model parameters, becomes less feasible. Using GPT-3 175B as an example – deploying independent instances of fine-tuned models, each with 175B parameters, is prohibitively expensive. We propose Low-RankAdaptation, or LoRA, which freezes the pretrained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the Transformer architecture, greatly reducing the number of trainable parameters for downstream tasks. Compared to GPT-3 175B fine-tuned with Adam, LoRA can reduce the number of trainable parameters by 10,000 times and the GPU memory requirement by 3 times. LoRA performs on-par or better than finetuning in model quality on RoBERTa, DeBERTa, GPT-2, and GPT-3, despite having fewer trainable parameters, a higher training throughput, and, unlike adapters, no additional inference latency. We also provide an empirical investigation into rank-deficiency in language model adaptation, which sheds light on the efficacy of LoRA. We release a package that facilitates the integration of LoRA with PyTorch models and provide our implementations and model checkpoints for RoBERTa, DeBERTa, and GPT-2 at https://github.com/microsoft/LoRA. Many applications in natural language processing rely on adapting one large-scale, pre-trained language model to multiple down-h stream applications. Such adaptation is

a future work. Practical Benefits and Limitations. The most significant benefit comes from the reduction in memory and storage usage. For a large Transformer trained with Adam, we reduce that VRAM usage by up to 2/3 ifr dmodel as we do not need to store the optimizer states for the frozen parameters. On GPT-3 175B, we reduce the VRAM consumption during training from 1.2TB to 350GB. Withr = 4 and only the query and value projection matrices being adapted, the checkpoint size is reduced by roughly 10,000× (from 350GB to 35MB)[^4]. This allows us to train with significantly fewer GPUs and avoid I/O bottlenecks. Another benefit is that we can switch between tasks while deployed at a much lower cost by only swapping the LoRA weights as opposed to all the parameters. This allows for the creation of many customized models that can be swapped in and out on the fly on machines that store the pre-trained weights in VRAM. We also observe a 25% speedup during training on GPT-3 175B compared to full fine-tuning[^5] as we do not need to calculate the gradient for the vast majority of the parameters. LoRA also has its limitations. Edward Hu∗ Yelong Shen∗ Phillip Wallis Zeyuan Allen-Zhu Yuanzhi Li Shean Wang Lu Wang Weizhu Chen yuanzhil, swang, luw, wzchen}@microsoft.com An important paradigm of natural language processing consists of large-scale pretraining on general domain data and adaptation to particular tasks or domains. As we pre-train larger models, full fine-tuning, which retrains all model parameters, becomes less feasible. Using GPT-3 175B as an example – deploying independent instances of fine-tuned models, each with 175B parameters, is prohibitively expensive. We propose Low-RankAdaptation, or LoRA, which freezes the pretrained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the Transformer architecture, greatly reducing the number of trainable parameters for downstream tasks. Compared to GPT-3 175B fine-tuned with Adam, LoRA can reduce the number of trainable parameters by 10,000 times and the GPU memory requirement by 3 times. LoRA performs on-par or better than finetuning in model quality on RoBERTa, DeBERTa, GPT-2, and GPT-3, despite having fewer trainable parameters, a higher training throughput, and, unlike adapters, no additional inference latency. We also provide an empirical investigation into rank-deficiency in language model adaptation, which sheds light on the efficacy of LoRA. We release a package that facilitates the integration of LoRA with PyTorch models and provide our implementations and model checkpoints for RoBERTa, DeBERTa, and GPT-2 at https://github.com/microsoft/LoRA. We release a package that facilitates the integration of LoRA with PyTorch models and provide our implementations and model checkpoints for RoBERTa, DeBERTa, and GPT-2 at https://github.com/microsoft/LoRA. For a large Transformer trained with Adam, we reduce that VRAM usage by up to 2/3 ifr dmodel as we do not need to store the optimizer states for the frozen parameters. On GPT-3 175B, we reduce the VRAM consumption during training from 1.2TB to 350GB. Withr = 4 and only the query and value projection matrices being adapted, the checkpoint size is reduced by roughly 10,000× (from 350GB to 35MB)[^4]. This allows us to train with significantly fewer GPUs and avoid I/O bottlenecks. Another benefit is that we can switch between tasks while deployed at a much lower cost by only swapping the LoRA weights as opposed to all the parameters. This allows for the creation of many customized models that can be swapped in and out on the fly on machines that store the pre-trained weights in VRAM. We also observe a 25% speedup during training on GPT-3 175B compared to full fine-tuning[^5] as we do not need to calculate the gradient for the vast majority of the parameters.
